# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: one-button canvas endless runner / simple driving arcade game.
- objective: start a run, tap/click/press Space or ArrowUp to jump a bus over traffic obstacles, collect rider pickups, and survive as speed increases.
- input model: mobile touchstart and mouse on the canvas trigger jump only while active and grounded; keyboard Space/ArrowUp also jump; start/restart are native buttons.
- core loop: initialize score/speed/entities, scroll city road, apply gravity, spawn hazards every 120 frames and pickups every 90 frames, test AABB contacts, add +5 on pickup, end immediately on obstacle contact.
- fail/friction state: collision with traffic stops the loop, hides HUD, shows final score and restart CTA; missed pickups simply scroll away.

## Protected mechanics
- Preserve one-thumb jump input, grounded-only jump gating, gravity value 0.6, jumpPower -12, bus dimensions, x anchor, and ground-relative placement.
- Preserve obstacle/passenger spawn cadence, random chance, movement by gameSpeed, speed escalation every 600 frames, AABB collision semantics, +5 pickup scoring, and immediate game-over on hazard contact.
- Preserve start, game-over, restart, HUD score, and mobile canvas touch handling without global touch suppression.

## Remixed target
A portrait-first vaporwave Y2K bus simulator satire titled Bus Simulator 2K where the same endless-runner bus route becomes a chrome neon-noir commute leaderboard run: the player is an alpha-route bus driver hopping traffic sludge, scooping cyber riders for clout, and chasing sweat-lord scores in fast mobile sessions.
